causative action by which humans or deities cause objects to be without curve or bend and/or have an even or regular surface
s.g: to make straight; to make smooth; to make level; to make even

s.d: action by which animals move forward without deviating to the left or the right
literally: to make one's way straight; = action by which humans move forward without deviating to the right or to the left; ≈ with the possible connotation of minding one's own affairs
s.g: to make straight one's way > to walk straight ahead

s.d: literally: to make straight one's eyelids; = action by which humans look forward without being distracted by things visible on the left or on the right
literally: to make someone else's way straight; = causative action by which deities cause the actions and endeavors of humans to be prosperous and successful
literally: to make straight; = causative action by which humans cause an action to be performed in a morally and ethically acceptable way
s.g: to make straight (an event) > to (perform an event) right

s.d: causative action by which humans cause water to flow in a certain direction
state in which humans are morally and ethically right
s.g: to be upright; to be just

s.d: literally: to be straight in the eyes of someone; hence: = state/process by which humans consider someone or something good
s.g: to be straight in the eyes (of someone) > to be accepted; to be approved; to please

s.d: state/process by which humans consider something morally and ethically right
man; ◄ son of {L:Caleb<SDBH:כָּלֵב>}; tribe of {L:Judah<SDBH:יְהוּדָה>}
state in which objects are without a bend or curve
literally: straight way; = journey without accidents or incidents
literally: straight way; = behavior that is morally and ethically right
state in which an event is morally and ethically right
person whose behavior is morally and ethically right
state in which humans are morally and ethically right
state in which an event is morally and ethically right

state in which humans are advanced in age

town; ◄ territory of {L:Dan<SDBH:דָּן>}
man; ◄ {L:from Moab<SDBH:מֹואָבִי>}; ► warrior; time of king {L:David<SDBH:דָּוִד>}

town; ◄ territory of {L:Judah<SDBH:יְהוּדָה>}
state in which humans, animals, plants, or objects remain in a certain place after part of the original quantity has disappeared or has been used or dealt with in a certain way
s.g: to remain; to be left behind; to be left over; to survive

s.d: causative action by which humans or deities cause humans, plants, or objects to remain in existence after part of the original quantity has disappeared or has been used or dealt with in a certain way
s.g: to cause to remain; to leave over

s.d: literally: no breath remains in (someone); hence: = process by which humans stop breathing and die
state in which time is left after part of the original span of time has passed
s.g: to be left over; to remain

s.d: state in which humans have a higher status than others
causative action by which deities cause humans to attain a state of great prosperity and success
what remains in a certain place after part of the original quantity has disappeared or has been used or dealt with in a certain way; used for humans, animals, plants, and inanimate objects
what remains in time after part of the original span of time has passed
events that have taken place, that are not among a range of events that have been described or dealt with in a certain way; used for acts of kings only
state in which humans have a higher status than others
state in which human speech is of an excellent quality
state in which an event is being done to a larger extent than is normally done
literally: what remains, or is left over; hence: = possessions that one has in surplus over the possession one needs in order to live
relatively thin string; ► used to hold a tent or similar construction in place, but also as bowstring; in Judges 16 used to tie down a person
literally: to pull up (someone's) tent-cord; hence: = causative action by which an end is made to a human life ◄ as if it were a tent of which the cords are pulled up so that it will collapse
s.g: to pull up (someone's) tent-cord > to cause someone to die

s.d: literally: to loosen (someone's) bowstring; hence: = causative action by which deities reduce the strength of humans and make them more vulnerable
s.g: to loosen (someone's bowstring) > to render (someone) weak, vulnerable

s.d: man, also known as {L:Jethro<SDBH:יִתְרֹו>} and {L:Reuel<SDBH:רְעוּאֵל>}; ► {L:priest<SDBH:כֹּהֵן>} of {L:Midian<SDBH:מִדְיָן>}; father-in-law of {L:Moses<SDBH:מֹשֶׁה>}
man; ◄ son of {L:Gideon<SDBH:גִּדְעֹון>}
man; ► father of {L:Amasa<SDBH:עֲמָשָׂא>}, army commander under {L:Absalom<SDBH:אַבְשָׁלֹום>} and {L:David<SDBH:דָּוִד>}, killed by {L:Joab<SDBH:יֹואָב>}

state in which an event is being done to a larger extent than is normally done
process by which an object increases in height
s.g: to become high; to be lifted up

s.d: process by which objects rise up from a certain location
causative action by which humans or forces take hold of objects and cause them to rise up from a certain location
s.g: to lift up; to raise; to raise up

s.d: literally: to lift up (one's heart or self) towards something or someone; hence: = action by which humans turn to a deity or location with the confidence that they will find help and support there
s.g: to count on; to be intent on; to desire

s.d: literally: to lift up (one's) face; hence: = action by which humans look up without shame
literally: to lift up (one's) head; hence: = action by which humans look up without shame
literally: to lift up (someone's) head; hence: = causative action by which humans declare other humans free after having held them prisoner

literally: to be lifted up = state in which humans or deities have an elevated status, either in their own eyes or in the eyes of other people, ≈ which can either be good or bad, depending on whether this status is justified
s.g: to be exalted; to be proud

s.d: literally: (one's) heart lifts (someone) up; hence: = process by which humans become arrogant in their thinking
literally: to lift up (one's) eyelids; hence: = action by which humans show that they consider themselves to have an elevated status, especially with their eyes
literally: to lift oneself up; hence: = action by which humans, deities, or groups ascribe greatness and authority to themselves
literally: to lift up (someone); hence: = causative action by which humans ascribe greatness and authority to humans, deities, or groups
literally: to arise; hence: = process by which an event starts happening
literally: to lift up; hence: = action by which humans take hold of objects with their hands, with the intention of holding them or bringing them to another location
s.g: to take; to take up; to lift up; to carry

s.d: state in which humans, animals, or objects are bearing a load while moving from one place to another
literally: to hold; hence: = process by which humans are held responsible for a certain action or for the well-being of others
literally: to cause to hold; hence: = causative process by which humans cause other humans to be held responsible for a certain action
literally: to bear; hence: = action by which humans or deities let go of any anger or resentment with regard to the wrongdoing or sin of (other) humans
literally: to hold; hence: = state in which an object or space is large enough to contain people or objects
s.g: to contain; to support; to hold

s.d: literally: to take (someone's) soul/self; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to die
literally: to take (someone's) away; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to die
s.g: to take away; to cause to die

s.d: literally: to hold, carry; hence: = state in which humans are dressed in a piece of clothing; ► used exclusively for the ephod worn by priests; ≈ associated with some level of responsibility as well

literally: to hold, carry; hence: = state in which humans hold something by attaching it to their clothes or by hiding it in the fold of their robes; ≈ often associated with carrying some amount of responsibility for something as well
literally: to hold, carry; hence: = process by which humans undergo certain processes or actions initiated by (other) humans or deities
s.g: to receive; to get; to undergo

s.d: literally: to take a wife (for oneself); hence: = action by which a man contracts a marriage with a woman for himself
literally: to take a wife (for someone else); hence: = action by which a man contracts a marriage with a woman on behalf of someone else
s.g: to take a wife (for someone else)

s.d: literally: to take the number (of a group); hence: = action by which humans try to determine the number of a group of people by having them counted
s.g: to number; to take a census

s.d: literally: to take the sum (of a group); hence: = action by which humans try to determine the number of a group of people by having them counted
s.g: to number; to take a census

s.d: literally: to cause to hold, carry; hence: = causative action by which humans take hold of objects and bring them to another location
s.g: to carry; to take; to bring

s.d: literally: to cause to hold, carry; hence: = causative action by which humans bring an object to another location by using a means of transportation like an animal, cart, ship, or even one's own shoulder
s.g: to bring; to convey; to transport

s.d: literally: to bring; hence: = causative action by which humans bring objects to (other) humans or deities as a gift
s.g: to bring; to present; to give

s.d: literally: to hold, carry; hence: = action by which human take possession of something belonging to someone else
literally: to hold, carry; hence: = action by which humans provide help and support to other humans
s.g: to care for; to assist; to help; to support

s.d: literally: to hold, carry; hence: = process by which plants or trees (or the area where they grow) produces branches or fruit
literally: to yield prosperity; hence: = process by which an area produces abundance of crops ► which results in wealth and prosperity
literally: to hold, carry; hence: = state in which humans are willing to listen to other humans
literally: to lift up (one's) hand; hence = action by which humans initiate a physical conflict with other humans
literally: to lift up (one's) head/horn; hence: = action by which nations make an effort to engage in a military conflict with others, usually after having been defeated before but not totally
s.g: to raise one's head; to raise one's horn

s.d: action by which an object is lifted or raised into the skies, so that it towers above other objects
s.g: to lift up; to reach the skies

s.d: literally: to lift up; hence: = causative process by which a certain condition is made less intense
literally: to lift up (one's) foot; hence: = action by which someone starts walking
literally, to lift up (someone's) face; hence: = action with which humans or deities favor one side in a dispute over the other
to lift up (one's) eye; hence: = action by which humans direct their eyes away from the ground so that they can see what is in the distance or in the sky
to lift up (one's) face; hence: = action by which humans direct their face away from the ground so that they can see what is in the distance or in the sky
literally: to lift up (one's) eyes (to); hence: = action by which humans turn to a deity or place with the confidence that they will find help and support there
literally: to lift up (one's) voice = action by which humans speak with a loud voice
literally: to lift up (words); hence: = action by which humans utter certain words
literally: to lift up (one's) wings; hence: = action by which birds or other flying creatures raise their wings in order to fly away
literally: to lift up (one's) hands; hence: = action by which humans raise their arms to receive out, beckon, bless, or pray
action by which an animal raises itself from a lying position
literally: to lift oneself up; hence: = action by which deities come in action after a time of inactivity
s.g: to lift up oneself = to come into action

s.d: literally: to lift (one's) hand; hence: = action by which deities intervene after a time of inactivity
literally: to lift oneself up; hence: = action by which humans rise up in opposition or armed resistance to their government or ruler

literally: to lift up (one's) hands; hence: = action by which humans make a solemn statement often calling on a higher power to confirm that what is said is true or to punish the speaker if it turns out not to be true
literally: to lift up the light (of one's) face (over someone else); hence: = action by which deities show favor to humans ◄ as if the deity causes the light emanating from his face to shine on them

literally: to lift up (someone's) face; hence: = action by which humans or deities show favor or respect to someone, ◄ as if by allowing someone who is looking down out of shame or humility to look up directly into one's face
s.g: to respect; to look upon or treat with favor; to honor

s.d: literally: (one's) heart lifts (someone) up; hence: = state in which humans are willing to carry out a specific task
action by which humans carefully investigate a location
causative action by which humans send other humans to carefully investigate a location
literally: to spy out; hence: = action by which humans increase their knowledge by processing a large quantity of information
literally: to spy out; hence: = action by which deities try to locate a certain place by a careful investigation of the surrounding area
literally: to spy out; hence: = action by which humans travel through a certain area, seemingly without a clear destination
literally: to roam after (one's own) heart; hence: = action by which humans pursue their own thoughts and wishes
literally: to cause to roam; hence: = causative action by which humans show other humans the course in life that they need to take
s.g: to guide; to show the way
